value: FTC FTC Act Section 5 data security/privacy enforcement; State Attorneys General State breach notification and consumer privacy laws; PCI Security Standards Council / card brands (private) PCI DSS via acquirer contracts, not a government regulator; CISA / DHS SRMA, Commercial Facilities Sector (Lodging subsector)
PCI SSC PCI DSS v4.0.1 (contractual standard)

Payment card data is the dominant regulated data type in hotels and restaurants, and the largest share of sector breaches involve POS/PMS card data. PCI DSS is the only prescriptive, externally validated control set these businesses are held to (contractually). There is no federal sector cyber statute; FTC Section 5 and state laws judge 'reasonableness', which PCI compliance evidences.

Payment card data (PAN, track data) at POS and PMS; Guest PII: passports/IDs, loyalty profiles, stay history; Employee PII and biometric time-clock data; Reservation and online-ordering account credentials; Guest Wi-Fi usage data

Property Management System (PMS); Point-of-sale (POS) and payment terminals; Central reservation system / channel manager; Online ordering and delivery integrations; Guest Wi-Fi and IPTV networks; Electronic door locks / key card systems; Loyalty/CRM platforms
PCI DSS validation for card payments

Lodging is a subsector of CISA's Commercial Facilities Sector (SRMA: DHS). PCI DSS is contractual, not law; merchant validation levels are set by card brands. No sector-specific federal AI rules were verified. All 50 states, DC and the territories have breach notification statutes with differing triggers, deadlines and regulator-notice duties. They are not enumerated here.
